cls: Tumor necrosis factor (TNF) blocker - soluble p75 TNF receptor fusion protein
quick: Use only if clearly needed; limited placental transfer at term
Low transfer into milk; may be used with caution
No direct interaction; moderate if on concurrent methotrexate
TB screening, infection signs, CBC, malignancy surveillance
summary: Etanercept is a dimeric soluble form of the p75 (75 kDa) TNF receptor fused to the Fc portion of human IgG1 that binds and neutralizes TNF-alpha and TNF-beta, blocking TNF-driven inflammation. It is given by subcutaneous injection for rheumatoid arthritis, psoriatic arthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, plaque psoriasis, and polyarticular juvenile idiopathic and juvenile psoriatic arthritis. The usual adult dose is 50 mg weekly. It carries a boxed warning for serious infections (including tuberculosis and opportunistic infections) and for malignancies, particularly lymphoma in children and adolescents.
indications: Moderately to severely active rheumatoid arthritis (alone or with methotrexate)
Chronic moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis (adults; children 4 years and older)
Moderately to severely active polyarticular juvenile idiopathic arthritis (2 years and older)
Juvenile psoriatic arthritis (2 years and older)

dosage.d: 50 mg subcutaneously once weekly (with or without methotrexate)
dosage.n: May be given as one 50 mg injection or two 25 mg injections

dosage.d: 50 mg subcutaneously twice weekly for 3 months, then 50 mg once weekly
dosage.n: Starting dose up to 50 mg twice weekly

dosage.c: Pediatric pJIA / juvenile PsA / pediatric psoriasis

admin: Administer by subcutaneous injection into thigh, abdomen or upper arm, rotating sites
Screen for and treat latent tuberculosis before starting; assess for active TB
Complete age-appropriate vaccinations before initiation; avoid live vaccines during therapy
Allow refrigerated product to reach room temperature before injecting; do not shake
Train patients/caregivers on aseptic self-injection technique and sharps disposal
moa: TNF is a pro-inflammatory cytokine central to the pathology of rheumatoid arthritis, juvenile idiopathic arthritis, psoriatic arthritis, ankylosing spondylitis and plaque psoriasis, with elevated levels in affected tissues. Etanercept is a dimeric fusion protein consisting of the extracellular ligand-binding portion of the human 75 kDa (p75) TNF receptor linked to the Fc domain of human IgG1. It competitively binds soluble TNF-alpha and TNF-beta (lymphotoxin-alpha), preventing their interaction with cell-surface TNF receptors and thereby rendering TNF biologically inactive and reducing inflammatory activity.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to etanercept or any component
relative: Active or chronic infection (including localized infection)
Latent or active tuberculosis until treated
Moderate to severe heart failure (NYHA III-IV)
History of demyelinating disease (MS, optic neuritis)
History of lymphoproliferative disease or recent malignancy

preg: Use only if clearly needed. Registry data do not reliably establish an association with major birth defects, and placental transfer at term is low. Consider that immunomodulation may affect the neonate; avoid live vaccines in infants exposed in utero for the first several months of life.
lact: Etanercept is present in human milk in very small amounts and is poorly absorbed orally by the infant; it may be used during breastfeeding when needed, weighing benefits and risks.
renal: No dosage adjustment is required in renal impairment.
hepatic: No dosage adjustment is required in hepatic impairment; screen for hepatitis B before therapy.

major: Live or live-attenuated vaccines - risk of disseminated infection; avoid during treatment
Anakinra - increased serious infection and neutropenia; do not combine
Abatacept and other biologic DMARDs - increased serious infection; do not combine
moderate: Other immunosuppressants (methotrexate, corticosteroids) - additive infection risk (combination with MTX is often intended)
Cyclophosphamide - possible increased risk of malignancy
minor: Substrates with narrow therapeutic index whose metabolism normalizes as inflammation resolves (e.g., warfarin, cyclosporine) - monitor
interactions.alcohol: No direct interaction; if taking concurrent methotrexate, limit alcohol due to hepatotoxicity risk.
interactions.diagnostics: May affect QuantiFERON/TB testing interpretation; can cause cytopenias and induce autoantibodies (ANA, anti-dsDNA).

common: Injection site reactions (erythema, itching, pain, swelling)
serious: Serious infections including tuberculosis, bacterial sepsis and invasive fungal infections
New onset or worsening congestive heart failure
Demyelinating disorders (MS, optic neuritis, transverse myelitis)
emergency: Severe cytopenia with bleeding or persistent fever

monitoring: Tuberculosis screening before treatment and surveillance during therapy
Signs and symptoms of infection at each visit
Neurologic evaluation if demyelinating symptoms occur
Cardiac status in patients with heart failure; periodic malignancy surveillance
counsel: This medicine lowers your immune defenses - report fever, cough, or any sign of infection promptly
You will be tested for tuberculosis before starting and watched during treatment
Do not have live vaccines while on etanercept; update vaccinations beforehand
Learn correct injection technique, rotate sites, and dispose of needles safely; mild injection-site reactions are common
Tell your doctor about heart problems, numbness/tingling, easy bruising, or any new lumps
pk: Clinical improvement typically over 1-2 weeks to 3 months
Median peak serum concentration about 48-60 hours after a single SC dose
Refrigerate at 2-8 C; do not freeze; protect from light; may be kept at room temperature once, briefly, per label
pearls: BOXED WARNING: serious infections (including TB and opportunistic pathogens) and malignancies (lymphoma in children/adolescents)
Always screen and treat latent TB before starting and stay alert for active TB during therapy
Discontinue if a serious infection or sepsis develops
Avoid live vaccines; update immunizations before initiation
Use caution in moderate-severe heart failure and in demyelinating disease
missed: If a dose is missed, inject it as soon as remembered, then resume the regular weekly schedule. Do not give two doses on the same day; if you are unsure, contact your healthcare provider.
overdose: No dose-limiting toxicities have been observed; single IV doses up to about twice the recommended dose were administered to volunteers without dose-limiting toxicity. There is no known antidote - observe and provide supportive care.
